unit.why: A single anecdote: the tsaddik's mother travels to R. Elimelekh's grave, the Maor va-Shemesh discourages her, and he reverses himself after his dead master rebukes him.

stories.start_quote: פ"א שמעתי ממנו זצ״ל שסיפר כי
stories.summary_en: On her way to R. Elimelekh's grave in Lizhensk, the tsaddik's mother spends Shabbat with the author of Maor va-Shemesh, who tells her not to go. His late master then comes to him and rebukes him, so he urges her to go and arranges a carriage to take her across the border.

tags.why: The plot turns on her journey to the grave of R. Elimelekh.

quotes: נסעה אמו תחי׳ לליזענסק על קבר הק׳ בעל נועם אלימלך
tags.why: The mother is the central actor and the traveller.
The tsaddik's mother is the protagonist.

quotes: תדע כי מורי ורבי בא אלי והקפיד עלי מאוד
tags.why: The dead R. Elimelekh appears to his disciple and speaks to him.

quotes: מורי ורבי בא אלי והקפיד עלי מאוד
tags.why: The night appearance is probably a dream, though the text does not say so.

quotes: מה לך שתסית את הצדקת הזאת לבל תסע על קברי
tags.why: The dead master corrects his disciple.

quotes: ובעזה״י תשיג שם כל חפצה ומשאלותה
tags.why: The tsaddik keeps his power to help petitioners at his grave.
The master is strict and displeased with his disciple.

quotes: והיתה שבתה בשבת בעיר חדש הסמוך לגבול
tags.why: The first exchange takes place during a Shabbat stay.
The tale is framed as told by the tsaddik himself.
